newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Rao gets reprieves against arrest.
newsitem.headline: India's Rao gets reprieves against arrest.

text.p: Former Indian prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao won reprieves against arrest in two cases of alleged forgery and bribery on Friday, two days after he was granted bail in a cheating case, court officials said.
The Delhi High Court, in separate hearings, granted bail to Rao in the two cases, effectively protecting him against arrest in any of the three criminal cases in which he has been charged.
Rao, 75, was instructed not to tamper with evidence or hamper the trial in the two cases relating to Friday's order.
His bail in the bribery case, in which he is accused of bribing four lawmakers belonging to a regional party to narrowly win a confidence vote in parliament in 1993, will be reviewed on November 20.

The bail in the forgery case was granted until the end of the trial. He is accused of seeking to defame former prime minister V.P. Singh by forging documents to show Singh's son held a bank account in the Carribean island of St Kitts.
Rao was given bail in a cheating case by another Delhi judge on Wednesday. He has been charged with cheating expatriate Indian Lakhubhai Pathak of $100,000 in 1983.
In the forgery and cheating cases, the former prime minister has been charged along with his one-time Hindu guru Chandraswami and the guru's aide, Kailash Nath Agarwal.
The Supreme Court on Thursday granted bail to Chandraswami and Agarwal, who are both being held in Delhi's Tihar Jail, in the cheating case.
The Delhi Court on Friday granted them bail in the forgery case as well.
Rao is the first former or serving prime minister to face criminal charges in India. He resigned as prime minister in May after his Congress party was defeated in general elections.
The three charges each carry maximum penalties of between five and seven years in jail.
Rao led the Congress party to its worst defeat in this year's general elections.

He resigned as party president in September after being named in the cheating case. But Rao has held on to his post as the Congress party's head in parliament, a job that gives him considerable leeway with Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
Deve Gowda's minority government needs the Congress party's continued support in parliament to beat off a relentless challenge by the main opposition rightwing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Deve Gowda has denied the BJP's claim that his government was going soft on the investigations against Rao.

The Congress party, divided over its support to Deve Gowda's five month-old government, has been debating Rao's continuing as head of the Congress Parliamentary Party, following the filing of the three cases against him.
